action: Seekom advises guests not to click links, pay or share card details in response to unexpected messages, and to contact the provider using official details.
date_note: Seekom's notice says it identified unauthorised access on 20 November 2026.
exec: Seekom says guest booking data may have been accessed, and its accommodation customers are advised to warn guests.
geo_basis: operator region (Kaipara District, Northland) as stated by the article
plain: Seekom, a booking system used by accommodation providers, says an unknown party accessed its platform. Some guests have had suspicious WhatsApp messages; Seekom says it cannot confirm a link to the incident.

sources.name: Seekom, Cyber Security Incident Update (page updated 25 Nov 2026)

summary: Seekom says it identified unauthorised access to iBex, its online booking and property management platform, on 20 November 2026, and that its investigation is ongoing. It says, preliminarily, that names, contact details, dates of birth and masked payment details may have been accessed. Kai Iwi Lakes Campground told the NZ Herald that WhatsApp payment messages did not come from the council. Seekom says it cannot confirm a link between those messages and the incident.
title: Seekom confirms unauthorised access to its iBex booking platform; Northland campgrounds warn customers

validation.note: Seekom's own notice (primary) and NZ Herald each state the breach.

review.note: Compared title, date, status, summary, action and sectors against the NZ Herald article: Seekom reported breach, Kai Iwi Lakes statement, Top 10 CEO remark and no Seekom statement all match; single_source is right.

evidence.quote: We identified unauthorised access to that platform on 20 November 2026.
